objective: Predict uninstrumented Cloud Run CPU nanoseconds of three previously unmeasured static CPP20 programs, using the fixed diagnostic probe and deterministic simple nonnegative models.
calibration: Use exactly the five established Cloud development families integer, branch, sort, rep_copy and rep_fill, scales 1, 2, 4, each with three native-before/v8-live/native-after brackets from the single new Seoul v8 revision. One equally weighted training row per (family,scale). For response use median of six native CPU ns. For predictors take medians of three diagnostic dual-client replays on exactly matching executable/stdin/oracle bytes. Use same diagnostic release and flags for training and prediction. Local archival counts may be reused if all tool and case digests match the same dedicated fixed-ASLR recipe. V8/cloud native CPU from diagnostic client never enters outcomes.
transformation: load_branch_interaction = integer floor square root of (load_instructions * gshare_mispredicts), per repetition. Nonnegative, monotone in each input. This aggregate feature does not measure which loads actually depend upon mispredicted branches. No intercept for any model.
fit: For each model and each fold, scale each input by training max (drop any zero column) and fit with scipy.optimize.nnls to relative-error design: normalized inputs divided by (case native median / median of training native medians), with target 1. Training is equal-weighted least squares on relative errors; freeze weights in ns/unit quantized round-to-nearest multiples of 1e-9. Predict integer ns by integer dot product and ceiling at 1e-9. No search or adjustment using external cases. Report the three fits once even if an interaction has zero weight.
development_check: Leave one whole training program out at a time and score all repetition vectors for that family. If a feature is absent from training it receives weight zero, record this explicitly. No fold result changes the fit or candidate.

external.release: Freeze and SHA256 timestamp each coefficient and prediction before receiving any prospective native outcomes or verdicts.

gates: For each external case all 3 interaction predictions must be within +/-20% of median of 6 native controls; report native duration >=20 ms and range/median <=10% and each input counter variation (max-min)/median <=0.1% separately; report actual errors regardless of repeatability. Compare linear and cheap controls on all external cases. No new model is qualified for Aonohako or used for verdicts, its live page lacks load/gshare counts.
fit_boundaries: Historic CSES, merge/hash, fresh holdout CPU or program label, and decision timing at 80%/120% are never fit inputs. No fitting on exposed outside workloads. No single-instruction cost conclusion from this empirical interaction.
